open_errors.issue: Chapters 13 to 15 say Kunal has watched Ila, and Ila has carried the queen's letter, for 'more than two weeks'. The pair bound at dawn after the Fair, and Ila received the letter the evening before. Chapter 17, several days later, counts day ten of the bond ('ten days of Ila's field book', 'ten strokes').
open_errors.fix: Bring the counts in chapters 13 to 15 down to six days roped and about a week carrying the letter.

patches.find: He had watched her for more than two weeks now and it had not once grown ordinary.
patches.replace: He had watched her for six days now and it had not once grown ordinary.

patches.find: But she had spent two weeks learning his habits.
patches.replace: But she had spent six days learning his habits.

patches.find: She had carried it for more than two weeks.
patches.replace: She had carried it for a week.

patches.find: I've carried it more than two weeks and haven't opened it.
patches.replace: I've carried it a week and haven't opened it.

open_errors.issue: At Ewe's Rest Ila judges Kunal 'happier than she had seen him in a fortnight'. She has known him for only a few days on the rope, plus two drafting-table sessions.

patches.find: looking happier than she had seen him in a fortnight.
patches.replace: looking happier than she had ever seen him.

open_errors.issue: Ila spent the summer surveying Neshar with Kiran. Her commission reached her 'with the summer post', and she wrote to the Taravan archive rather than visit it. Yet chapter 3 has her buying the rope in Taravan in the autumn, and chapter 6 has her reading the commission 'a dozen times in Taravan'.
open_errors.fix: Have her send to Taravan for the rope, and read the commission after it arrived by post.

patches.find: She had bought the rope in Taravan in the autumn, undyed wool from Lata's house, spun to a hand's thickness.
patches.replace: She had sent to Taravan for the rope in the autumn, undyed wool from Lata's house, spun to a hand's thickness.

patches.find: She had read the paper a dozen times in Taravan, and once more by lamp in the guest-house, and she knew every word.
patches.replace: She had read the paper a dozen times since the summer post, and once more by lamp in the guest-house, and she knew every word.

open_errors.issue: In chapter 1, Tamar's Shoulder is a name Ila has hand-lettered on her current summer sheets of the Neshar passes, for 'the cook who had fed her at seven'. In chapter 6 she says she named it at seven and that it is 'on the family map'.
open_errors.fix: Keep the cook from her seventh year and put the name on her summer sheets.

patches.find: After a cook who fed me. I was seven. It's still on the family map.
patches.replace: After a cook who fed me when I was seven. It's on my summer sheets.

open_errors.issue: Chapter 20 treats Ila calling him 'Kunal' as new, as if she had always said 'Highness'. She has called him Kunal throughout, from chapter 3 on ('Kunal, what's that?').
open_errors.fix: Make the moment about the tone in which she says it, not about her first use of the name.

patches.find: Not *Highness*. Not *the prince*, with the small, dry edge she kept on it. His own name, in her brisk voice.
patches.replace: Not *Highness*, the word she still kept for distance. His own name, and nothing brisk in it at all.

open_errors.issue: In chapter 21 Kunal watched Ila sew the sheets into her pattu's side seam. In chapter 24 he thinks they are 'somewhere about her; he had never asked where', but in chapter 26 he again knows they are sewn in.
open_errors.fix: Let Kunal remember watching her sew them in.

patches.find: Five sheets with every turn of the hills drawn true, somewhere about her; he had never asked where.
patches.replace: Five sheets with every turn of the hills drawn true, sewn into her pattu's seam; he had watched her stitch them in.

open_errors.issue: Gauri is introduced in chapter 7 as 'a tall woman'. In chapter 27 she is 'small and broad'.

patches.find: The shape in the cleft mouth was small and broad.
patches.replace: The shape in the cleft mouth was tall and broad.

open_errors.issue: Raghu had eight bound pairs in all: six in the bowl and two on the Kuhl shoulder. Raghu's own pair and the cornice pairs left for the Drum, and one pair drowned. Pasang still says 'Eight pairs watch the doors' at the Hollow Moon huts.
open_errors.fix: Reduce the guard to what is left.

patches.find: Hari's with them. Eight pairs watch the doors.
patches.replace: Hari's with them. Six pairs watch the doors.

open_errors.issue: Kunal's right fingertips died from his broken promise at the herders' hut in chapter 21, before the cleft was entered. Chapter 31 says they have been grey 'since the Eye'.
open_errors.fix: Date the dead tips to the broken promise.

patches.find: His fingertips stayed grey, as they had been since the Eye.
patches.replace: His fingertips stayed grey, as they had been since the morning he broke his promise.
